title: Swearing by Saints is as forbidden as sacrificing to them
source_text: XXVII. Similiter omnino improbant consuetudinem jurandi per Sanctos, nec minus vetitum censent per creaturas quaslibet jurare, quam illis sacrificare, quoniam Scriptura non minus illos damnat, qui jurant per eos qui Dii non sunt, quam illos qui offerunt sacrificium praeterquam Deo soli. Nec plus rationis vident ut secundario juretur per Sanctos, quatenus in iis elucet divina veritas, quam ut iis secundario quoque sacrificetur, quatenus in illis apparent insignia Omnipotentiae & Bonitatis divinae documenta.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise they altogether disapprove the custom of swearing by the Saints, and they judge it no less forbidden to swear by any creatures than to sacrifice to them, since Scripture no less condemns those who swear by those who are not gods than those who offer sacrifice to any but God alone. Nor do they see more reason that one should swear secondarily by the Saints, insofar as divine truth shines in them, than that one should also sacrifice to them secondarily, insofar as notable proofs of divine omnipotence and goodness appear in them.
pass_b_english: Swearing by the Saints is rejected outright.
An oath by any creature is as forbidden as a sacrifice to that creature, because Scripture condemns both swearing by what is not God and sacrificing to any but God.
A secondary oath, on the ground that divine truth shines in the Saints, has no more excuse than a secondary sacrifice on the ground that God's power and goodness appear in them.

choices.why: The scriptural ban is on oaths by non-gods, not only on oaths that name the Saint as supreme.
rejected: oaths by God's name alone are the only issue
